one_line: Roadside construction yard beside the Luxor-Aswan desert road: graded pale pad with shed, cabins, berm and access track seen in 2025 Esri imagery.
summary: before.png (median of 2023-04-25 to 2023-08-13) shows uniform orange desert in the yellow box, faintly gridded into plots, with the dark dual carriageway of the Luxor-Aswan Western Road about 150-170 m to the east; after.png (median of 2024-05-19 to 2024-09-06) shows a bright cream patch filling most of the box plus new blue-grey roadside patches about 200 m north, and difference.png shows the footprint as an isolated compact brightening block (+0.04 and more) with only a weak NDVI dip. hires.png (Esri, acquired 2025-05-07, 1.09 m) resolves the box as a pale graded rectangle with an access track running north-east to the road, and a 0.54 m zoom chip of the same image shows a white-roofed shed about 25 x 10 m, two or three small blue-roofed cabins, a roughly 40 m berm or wall casting a shadow, a cluster of planted trees, tyre tracks and blue-grey stained ground: a small desert worksite or contractor yard. wayback_strip.png shows the spot as undisturbed desert in the releases published 2014, 2017, 2019, 2022 and 2023-12-07 and the same graded yard in the 2026-05-28 release; OSM already maps a 161 m highway=service way (1230530633) touching the footprint, with the Cairo-Abu Simbel high-speed railway under construction 278 m away. timeseries.png shows inside-footprint brightness tracking the ring until mid-2023 and then ramping over about nine months (inside-minus-ring contrast +0.010 in Aug 2023 to +0.100 in May 2024) with NBR rising in step, a staged build-up rather than a single event, confirmed independently by Landsat (+0.041) and present in 12 of 12 later Sentinel-2 scenes; the spectra (d_brightness +0.084, d_nbr +0.082, d_swir +0.016, d_ndvi -0.022) are those of pale dry exposed or compacted fill, not burn, water or snow, on a flat (0.9 deg) hyperarid plain. All three sceptics (human activity, natural processes, artefacts) independently refuted the candidate with high confidence on the same evidence, and the panel concludes it is an ordinary graded construction yard beside a trunk road in an active construction corridor; the buildings, berm and track are directly seen, the yard's exact purpose is inferred.
explanation: Ordinary earthworks: a small desert worksite or contractor yard graded on a roadside plot between about August 2023 and May 2024, beside the Luxor-Aswan Western Road (trunk, 163 m) and 278 m from the Cairo-Abu Simbel high-speed railway under construction. The Esri image of 2025-05-07 (hires.png and its 0.54 m zoom) shows the graded pale pad with a white-roofed shed, blue-roofed cabins, a berm, planted trees, tyre tracks and an access track to the road, the track already mapped in OSM as service way 1230530633 touching the footprint; the five Wayback releases through 2023-12-07 show undisturbed desert there. The brightening is exposed pale compacted fill or subsoil. The yard's specific purpose (HSR contractor yard, land-reclamation plot or well site) is inferred.
next_step: A single dated image between September 2023 and May 2024 (a Sentinel-2 chip from 2023-09-27, 2023-11-11 or 2024-01-30, or a Planet/Maxar scene) at 24.5329 N 32.7294 E to watch the pad, berm and buildings appear stage by stage; or the OSM history of service way 1230530633 and any later landuse tag to name the yard's purpose. Neither is needed to exclude an extraordinary cause, which the 2025-05-07 Esri image already does.
